segments.title: Inside Hikawa Maru's preserved engine room
segments.summary: Hikawa Maru's well-maintained engine room lets visitors examine the large diesel machinery that carried the ship on its Seattle route.
segments.body: The visit begins below decks in Hikawa Maru's engine room, where the large diesel engines can be examined closely. The machinery is described as especially well maintained and displayed so visitors can see how it works. Its scale gives physical context to the power needed to carry the ship to Seattle. This stop makes the propulsion system part of the vessel's history instead of leaving it as an abstract technical detail. For this visit, the engine room is reason enough to see the ship.

evidence.note: He tours the engine room, describes the large diesel engines, and explains that the ship is well maintained for visitors.

segments.title: Hikawa Maru and Seattle's maritime connection
segments.summary: Hikawa Maru belonged to the NYK Line shipping network that linked Seattle with the wider world.
segments.body: A remark attributed to a Seattle mayor called the Great Northern the city's father and the NYK Line its mother. Hikawa Maru and similar ships supplied the physical connection behind that comparison by linking Seattle with the wider world. The point shifts attention from the preserved vessel alone to the shipping network it once served. It offers a concise explanation of how passenger liners and commercial routes connected Pacific ports. Preserving Hikawa Maru also preserves evidence of that urban and international maritime history.

evidence.note: He identifies the NYK Line as a link between Seattle and the wider world and says ships such as Hikawa Maru made that connection possible.
